title: Types of hazard maps
---
::: {.callout-tip}
The most advised format for both event and risk is netCDF.
:::

```{python}
#| include: false

import os
from IPython.display import display
from pathlib import Path

os.chdir(Path.cwd().parent.parent.parent)
```

## Event
Event maps are generally supplied in singular fashion (i.e. one band per event map).
This band just simply contains the hazard values per cell. Let's have a quick peek at the data:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.grid-output-scroll}
```{python}
#| echo: false
from fiat.open import open_grid
# Open the file
ds = open_grid("data/event_map.nc")
# Show an overview of the data
display(ds)
# Show a variable and it's metadata
display(ds[0])
```
:::
::::
::: {.callout-note}
Although netCDF is the preferred format, GeoTIFF's are also very handy for single events.
:::

As one can see, this dataset has only one band (variable).

When created, it is preferred that the event map is compressed to prevent unneccessary data on the hard drive.
More information regarding the compression of netCDF files and others settings can be found [here](https://www.unidata.ucar.edu/blogs/developer/entry/netcdf_compression).

## Risk
Risk maps in gerenal should contain multiple bands.

Lets take a look quick look at the data:

:::: {.columns}
::: {style="height: 400px; overflow: auto;"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
!gdalinfo ../../../data/hazard/risk_map.nc
```
:::
::::
::: {.callout-note}
Instead of seeing normal metadata, we only get an overview of the available subdatasets.
:::

Multiple netCDF variables are normally not recognized as bands by the [netCDF driver](https://gdal.org/drivers/raster/netcdf.html) of GDAL.
Instead they are interpreted as subdatasets (!). One can set the key `var_as_band` to `true` within the [settings file](../settings/index.qmd)
to read the subdatasets as bands.

```toml
[hazard]
file = <your-file>
risk = true
[hazard.settings]
var_as_band = true
```

When supplied in one subdataset (all bands are within that subdataset),
the `subset` variable within the [settings file](../settings/index.qmd) should be set under the header `hazard.settings`.
The value set to `subset` should be the name of the desired subdataset.

```toml
[hazard]
file = <your-file>
risk = true
[hazard.settings]
var_as_band = false
subset = <your-wanted-subdataset>
```

### Return periods

The return period of a band is set per band in the [settings file](../settings/optional.qmd#hazard.variables) with the `rp` entry
of a `[[hazard.variables]]` entry (required for every band in a risk calculation), see [hazard settings](hazard.qmd#settings).
An `rp` attribute of the band in the file is not read.

Every return period needs a band of every hazard type required by the [methods](vulnerability.qmd#methods)
of the linked vulnerability datasets (e.g. a `water_depth` and a `flood_duration` band per return period).

Let's have a quick peek at the data using [gdalinfo](https://gdal.org/programs/gdalinfo.html) (it will be at the bottom):

:::: {.columns}
::: {style="height: 400px; overflow: auto;"}
```{python}
#| echo: false
!gdalinfo -sd 1 -norat -nogcp ../../../data/hazard/risk_map.nc
```
:::
::::
